taglineHtml: I study computer science and artificial intelligence. Everything published here is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed. This place has one core: auditing, by machine, what I have already published. The three Trinity-Infinity papers are what it was applied to. Three papers in philosophy and a source note are in Notes; certificates and areas of study are in CV.

claim.statementHtml: A published artifact cannot be revised. Only the errata can. So the errata drifts away from its source over time. A quotation loses a word, occurrences are undercounted, an item declared unresolvable is quietly marked resolved. That drift can be caught by machine, without inference.
claim.statement: corrections drift from their sources, and the drift is machine-detectable

rows.term: What the three papers came to
rows.html: The framework did not survive. What remains is one fact about one operator: for Q an n-cycle and D diagonal, (DQ)ⁿ = (∏ᵢ aᵢ)·I exactly, so convergence is governed by the geometric mean of the coefficients — not by their maximum, and not by the operator norm.The fact is correct, machine-checked, and at the level of a second- or third-year undergraduate exercise. The error is the confusion that course sets on its exam. Only the tool used to repair the proof belongs to graduate linear systems and matrix analysis: the transient growth of a non-normal matrix (the error swells 11.8× at step 2) and the construction of a contracting norm from a Lyapunov equation. The level of the tool and the level of what it repaired are two different things. The closest department is not numerical analysis but linear systems and control: the object is the asymptotic stability of a discrete-time system. Of the symbol Ⅲ∞, the half with mathematical content (Ⅲ, three) is the half that was proved not to matter. The route is recorded here.

The tool was not built first and then pointed at a paper. It came out of auditing my own three papers. The undercount, the characters added to a quotation that are not in the original, and the last-updated stamp that was older than a date inside the document were all found in my own records.

I believed the three papers promised a bundled verification script in three places. Counting the pages, there are six. That was found by machine, not by reading. 78 checks on the errata itself, 68 on the tool. The tool is checked by breaking a passing state in 26 distinct ways and asserting that each break fails exactly the corresponding check.

The frozen papers are run through the Stanford Agentic Reviewer (paperreview.ai, built by Yixing Jiang and Andrew Ng), and every point it raises is checked one by one and recorded. What it got right and what it got wrong are both kept.It is not peer review. It grounds its reviews in arXiv, which puts these papers on the side where its accuracy is lower — that caveat is recorded alongside the reviews (in Japanese). One review independently found E6; another invented a typo that does not exist.

claim.refuteHtml: (1) Show one case that passes these checks while the errata does in fact diverge from its source. (2) Or show one check that does not fail when broken as declared. Either one refutes it. The declaration format and the break tests are in errata-check.
claim.footHtml: The volume of verification says nothing about the value of what is verified. No check in this system can decide that question. However many pass, none of them can ever report that the work is not worth doing. It is falsifiable at the level of claims and structurally unfalsifiable at the level of significance. That is recorded as unresolved (ST-002).

verification.note: How many checks, where, and when. All of them run in CI on every push. The first three are the core.

items.name: 213 checks on the errata
items.html: The same audit applied to all four frozen bodies of work: 78 on the three Trinity-Infinity papers, 95 on the three philosophical papers, 40 on the naval gazette source note. Every quotation verbatim, everything declared absent really absent, no quiet resolution of an item declared unresolvable, and the PDFs themselves unchanged (errata-check 10.5281/zenodo.22649899)

items.name: 68 checks on the tool itself
items.html: A checking tool cannot be trusted merely because it passes; a tool that looks at nothing passes too. A passing state is broken in 26 distinct ways, and each break must fail exactly the corresponding check. The distributions used to recompute p are validated against published statistical tables at eleven points (errata-check)

items.name: 34 checks on the register
items.html: The shape and history of the correction record itself. 57 entries across five statuses, 30 of them reconstructed after the fact and marked as such, with the recording date checked against git history. 49 can be checked by anyone against a frozen artifact; the remaining 8 rest on the author’s word alone, and that too is a field. That standing claims carry a refutation route, that unresolvable items give a reason, and that no entry ever published has since been removed (self-correction)

items.name: 31 printed numbers
items.html: Every number printed in the three papers, recomputed and shown beside the printed value (trinity-infinity/verification/claims_audit.py)

items.name: 13 theorems reimplemented
items.html: The theorems reimplemented independently of the papers (trinity-infinity/verification/independent_check.py)

items.name: 29 checks on the operator
items.html: The operator outside the papers' assumptions, with a fixed seed (trinity-operator)

items.name: 51 checks on the certificate
items.html: The repaired argument itself: that P solves the Lyapunov equation, that ‖·‖_P is a norm, and that f contracts in that distance — checked from the definitions (trinity-operator)

items.name: 63 checks on the outlook
items.html: Which of the papers’ conclusions survive as each assumption is dropped. What is settled exactly, what is only estimated, and what is undecidable in principle, counted separately (trinity-operator/roadmap)

items.name: 90 checks in this page
items.html: The numerics behind the operator page, checked against 728 recorded NumPy results. Maximum relative difference: ρ 6.7×10⁻¹⁵, ‖A‖₂ 1.7×10⁻¹⁵. The constructed distance is checked against 23 recorded certificates as well (κ within 3.9×10⁻¹⁶)

papers.title: Trinity-Infinity Framework, Series I
papers.subtitle: A Conceptual Model with Illustrative Applications in Game Theory, Mathematical Logic, and Mechanical Engineering
papers.summary: Proves that the three-element recursive operator converges geometrically to a unique fixed point, and sets out the connections to game theory, logic and engineering with proved results, known results and analogies marked apart.

papers.title: Trinity-Infinity Framework, Series II
papers.subtitle: Extended Formalization and Further Illustrative Applications
papers.summary: Shows that uniqueness of the fixed point survives when the mixing rate varies coordinate by coordinate, and adds a characterization of the equilibrium payoff set and a fully worked spring-network example.

papers.title: Trinity-Infinity Framework, Series III
papers.subtitle: Beyond Three — A Generalization and Retrospective
papers.summary: Shows that the convergence theorem does not need three elements — it holds for any n ≥ 2 — and looks back at what the series established and what it withdrew.

works.title: errata-check
works.summary: Audits an errata document against a frozen, already-published artifact. Every quotation verbatim, no undercounting, no quiet resolution of an item declared unresolvable, and the artifact itself unchanged. Recomputation of p from printed test statistics, the GRIM test, ORCID/ISBN/ISSN check digits and Japanese era years can also be declared. No inference is used in the judgement, so the output does not need to be re-verified by a human.

works.title: self-correction
works.summary: Every claim I have published that turned out to be wrong, was withdrawn, or cannot be fixed — recorded one by one and never deleted. 57 entries so far. Five statuses only; standing claims must carry a refutation route and unresolvable ones must say why. Identifiers can never be removed: the check walks the git history and fails if any entry that was ever published has since disappeared.

works.title: Run the operator
works.summary: A page that iterates the operator x ← DQx + (I−D)p from the three papers above. Type in a matrix and it reports both the spectral radius and the operator norm, judges convergence and monotone decay separately, and draws the fixed point and the error curve. Where the papers' argument breaks, it constructs a distance in which f is a contraction and rebuilds the argument until Banach's theorem applies literally. Eigenvalues, singular values and the Lyapunov equation are all solved inside the page. No outbound requests.

works.title: trinity-infinity
works.summary: The three papers above and their verification. 15 checks that reimplement the theorems independently and 32 that recompute every number printed on the page. It also records what was established and what was withdrawn.

works.title: trinity-operator
works.summary: The operator from the three papers above, implemented without restricting Q to a permutation or the coefficients to a uniform scalar. Convergence is governed by the spectral radius; the operator-norm condition the papers impose is stronger than it needs to be. 22 checks, including an example whose error swells to 11.8× before it converges, 51 more on the construction that repairs the broken argument, and 63 on a staged outlook that drops one assumption at a time.

trinity-operator
@graph.description: The operator from the three Trinity-Infinity papers, implemented without restricting Q to a cyclic permutation or the coefficients to (0,1). It shows that convergence is governed by the spectral radius ρ(DQ) < 1, that the operator-norm condition the papers impose is merely sufficient, and that non-normal matrices amplify the error transiently. It also repairs the Banach argument that fails in that region by constructing a weighted norm from the Lyapunov equation, and lays out, as runnable stages, which conclusions survive as each assumption is dropped.

@graph.name: 作用素を回す
@graph.description: A tool that iterates the operator x ← DQx + (I−D)p from the three Trinity-Infinity papers entirely inside the browser. It reports the spectral radius and the operator norm separately, and judges convergence and monotone decay of the error as separate questions. Where the papers' argument does not hold, it solves the Lyapunov equation to construct a weighted norm in which the map contracts, and reports the contraction constant and the resulting error bound. Eigenvalues by Householder reduction and shifted QR, singular values by Jacobi rotation, linear systems by Gaussian elimination with partial pivoting, and Cholesky factorization — all without external libraries. No outbound requests. The interface is in Japanese.
